speaker: Dr Charlene Chen
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) in the past two years, how many complaints of age discrimination have been lodged with the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) and the Ministry; (b) how many of such cases are detected beyond formal complaints received; (c) which sectors are most frequently implicated; and (d) when is the Workplace Fairness Act expected to take effect.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In addition to the complaints received, TAFEP partners Workforce Singapore (WSG) to proactively review job advertisements posted on MyCareersFuture (MCF) portal to detect potentially discriminatory job advertisements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: TAFEP had engaged the employers that posted these job advertisements to make the necessary amendments to ensure alignment with the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (TGFEP).

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: For example, is there any data that happens more of hiring promotions or retrenchments?

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: And the second supplementary question is, how will MOM ensure that older workers, especially those less familiar with reporting channels, feel safe and supported to surface cases of discrimination?

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: And my last supplementary question is about the Workplace Fairness Act.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: When it comes into force, are there any safeguards that will ensure that enforcement is not just reactive, but also proactive in deterring unfair practices before they occur?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In terms of trend, our annual fair employment practice reports have not shown an uptrend over the past five years.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On the second question of how we ensure that there are adequate avenues, especially for those who may have challenges navigating the resources, I would say there are several avenues.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: One, of course, is we try to encourage those who have grievances to approach TAFEP, because there will be a team of mediators and staff who can help take the case into consideration and advise them on what recourse and avenues are open to them.
That is a proactive way to ensure that there are no misunderstandings on what is required.
Oftentimes, we see that when complaints surface, it may not necessarily be that the employers are egregious in trying to discriminate against a particular age group.
